error_type_detail: E4-S4 AC3: the interaction the contract's steps describe (fill all but one question, click Submit, see an inline validation message) cannot occur, because Submit is genuinely HTML-disabled whenever any question is unanswered, and a real click event never fires against a disabled native <button>.
expected: steps: fill_all_but_one -> click button[type=submit] -> assert no POST /api/risk-profile/submit is issued -> snapshot: an inline validation message is visible next to the unanswered question.
actual: Reproduced live with a real Chromium session, logged in as carol.singh@wealthwise.test: answered 5 of 6 questions, confirmed via page.evaluate that Submit still carries the disabled attribute (isDisabled()=true). A real (non-force) Playwright click against the button timed out after 30000ms with the log 'waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable ... element is not enabled' - the click never reaches the DOM's click event at all, so handleSubmit (which is the only place invalidQuestionIds is ever set) never runs. Result: postIssued=false (trivially true, since nothing can be submitted) but invalidCount=0 and errRoleAlertCount=0 - no inline validation message ever appears, because the code path that would produce it is structurally unreachable via a disabled button.
stack_trace: frontend/src/pages/customer/Questionnaire.tsx:167 - <button type="submit" disabled={!allAnswered || isSubmitting}>. `allAnswered` (line 120) is false whenever any question lacks an answer, which includes the 'all but one' state this check exercises - not just the fully-empty state. The `invalidQuestionIds` state (line 26, rendered at lines 141/160-164) is set exclusively inside `handleSubmit` (lines 71-100), which is only invoked by a real submit/click event - one that a disabled button structurally cannot dispatch.
test_coverage_gap: ut-200 (Questionnaire.test.tsx) presumably drives this via React Testing Library's fireEvent/userEvent, which in some configurations can dispatch a submit event programmatically even against a disabled button (jsdom is more permissive here than a real browser) - masking this gap at the unit-test layer. Only a real browser (this check) surfaces it.
note_for_generator: This is a genuine design tension between AC1 ('Submit disabled until all are answered') and AC3 ('inline validation on submit of an incomplete set') as literally specified - the current implementation satisfies AC1 by making AC3's exact interaction impossible. Two ways to reconcile, either is reasonable: (a) keep Submit enabled at all times and move the completeness gate entirely into handleSubmit's existing validation branch (which already exists and works correctly - it's just unreachable), removing the `disabled={!allAnswered}` clause; or (b) treat AC1's fully-disabled behavior as the intended, stronger UX and get the contract/AC3 text corrected to match (e.g. re-scope AC3 to describe the always-visible per-question 'answer required' hint state rather than a post-click validation flash). Not fixed by this evaluator per policy - flagging the tradeoff for whoever owns the fix.

error_type_detail: E10-S4 AC5: the version-history table does not reliably show the version just published immediately after a successful Publish click - it lags one version behind, even though the server has already committed and returned 201 for the new version before the refetch fires.
expected: Publishing a new template version calls POST /api/admin/allocation-templates (201), then the displayed version-history list immediately includes the new version, without a full page navigation/reload.
actual: Reproduced live and reproducibly across 3 independent Chromium sessions (Playwright 1.63.0), each publishing a fresh MODERATE-band template version in sequence: (1) published version 8 - DB confirmed id=12/version=8/is_active=true via direct curl immediately after, but the page's own history table still showed only 7 rows (pre-publish count) even after a 15x200ms poll loop; (2) same script re-run, after waiting 2s for any initial-mount fetch races to settle before publishing (to rule out a StrictMode double-effect explanation) - published version 10, DB confirmed id=14/version=10/is_active=true, but the page's history table still showed the PRIOR run's version 9 as its last row; (3) captured the exact network response body of the GET /api/admin/allocation-templates?risk_band=MODERATE request fired by loadHistory() immediately after a successful publish (response captured via page.waitForResponse, not just DOM inspection) - it returned 10 rows ending at version 10, while a direct DB read taken seconds later (once the script exited) already showed version 11 (id=15) committed and active. The POST's own 201 response (awaited before loadHistory() is called) reported 'Published version 11 for MODERATE' - i.e. the write itself completed and was acknowledged before the read-refresh was triggered, yet the read-refresh's response was missing that same write.
stack_trace: frontend/src/pages/admin/TemplateEditor.tsx:60-64 (loadHistory) and :101-116 (handlePublish) - `await publishAllocationTemplate(...)` completes, then `loadHistory(riskBand)` is called fire-and-forget (not awaited, and its own `.then(setHistory)` has no request-sequence guard). Compare to the sibling `assetClasses` fetch effect at lines 41-58, which does guard against a stale response via a `cancelled` closure flag - `loadHistory` has no equivalent, so if any other in-flight GET to the same endpoint (e.g. one still pending from the initial-mount useEffect, itself possibly double-fired by React 18 StrictMode in this dev build) resolves after the publish-triggered one, its older payload silently overwrites the fresher `history` state. Given the observed one-version lag is consistent rather than random, the true root cause may instead be on the backend side (a read-your-writes consistency gap between the POST's write transaction and the immediately following GET's read transaction/connection) rather than purely a frontend race - both a frontend request-ordering guard and a backend read-consistency check are worth investigating.
files_likely_involved: frontend/src/pages/admin/TemplateEditor.tsx:60-64,101-116 (no request-sequencing guard on loadHistory, unlike the assetClasses effect's `cancelled` pattern)
backend/src/app/routers/admin.py (GET /api/admin/allocation-templates handler - worth checking for a stale read after the sibling POST's write in the same test sequence)

backend/src/domain/admin/service.py / backend/src/domain/recommendation/repository.py (publish_template's write path - worth checking whether the write is fully flushed/committed before the POST handler returns 201)
